summary: 10 Minute School (10MS), a Bangladeshi edtech that began as a YouTube channel, raised a $5.5 million pre-Series A, the largest seed-stage round for a Bangladeshi startup so far, bringing its total to $7.5 million. It offers K12 supplementary education through a smartphone app, aiming to give rural students affordable access to quality teachers and content. The funds will go toward AI-driven personalization, content for Bangladesh's changing national curriculum, and a possible hybrid online/offline model.
one_line: Bangladeshi edtech 10 Minute School raised a record $5.5M pre-Series A to expand affordable, app-based K12 education beyond Dhaka.
key_facts: 10 Minute School (10MS) raised a pre-Series A of $5.5 million, the highest seed-stage funding so far for a Bangladeshi startup, bringing its total raised to $7.5 million.

The round was led by Conjunction Capital, with participation from Peak XV's Surge (formerly Sequoia Capital India), Startup Bangladesh Limited, CRED founder Kunal Shah, MyAsiaVC managing partner Sajid Rahman and local angel investors.
Ayman Sadiq started 10MS as a YouTube channel in 2015; he has taught since 2012 and was previously a teacher at a leading coaching center in Dhaka.
10MS has 35,000 recorded video lessons and over 82,000 quizzes, plus model tests, ebooks and lecture notes covering the entire national curriculum.
52% of 10MS students are from rural and semi-urban areas outside Dhaka, and 34% are girls.
Between 2015 and 2019 the YouTube channel took on sponsors and produced more than 25,000 videos covering the entire K12 syllabus; sponsors began dropping out when the pandemic hit.
10MS's first premium product, a paid book and course, individually had more than 100,000 paid users, which showed the company it could monetize.
In 2022, 10MS raised $2 million in seed funding led by Surge, Sequoia India's (now Peak XV) scale-up program.
10MS plans to invest in tech, content and operations, using AI for personalized learning and hiring more engineers and product managers.
10MS is exploring a hybrid online/offline model with after-school education centers and a new vertical for English material with a separate sales team.

Shikho, which focuses on elementary learners, previously held the seed-stage record with $5.3 million as of March 2022; Beg says 10MS has the advantage of being older, larger and teaching more grades.
Bangladesh has 42 million students enrolled in the K12 system, according to co-founder Mirza Salman Hossain Beg, and most lack access to quality teachers and content.
Conjunction Capital's Kirill Kozhevnikov said this is the firm's first venture into the Bangladesh market.
